name: @splitsutra/core
description: Platform-agnostic core for SplitSutra: types, schemas, domain logic, repositories, hooks. No DOM, no react-dom, no react-native.
//entry-points: These point at dist/, NOT at src/. This package used to name its TypeScript source as its entry points, which works for apps/web (Vite transpiles core) and fails for firebase/functions (real Node, ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on the .js specifiers core's imports carry, which nothing ever emitted). Every gate in the repo passed in that state. `tsconfig.build.json` explains the rest. apps/web is unaffected by the change either way: vite.config.ts and apps/web/tsconfig.json both alias @splitsutra/core straight to source, so `pnpm dev` needs no build and HMR still crosses the package boundary.
//files: src ships alongside dist so the .d.ts.map files emitted by tsconfig.build.json resolve — without it, "go to definition" from a consumer lands on generated declarations instead of the real source.
//devDependencies: react and its types are here only so this package can typecheck and BUILD itself. react is an OPTIONAL peer (see peerDependenciesMeta) because domain, types and utils have nothing to do with React and firebase/functions consumes them without it; src/hooks does import it, and without @types/react resolvable from this package tsc reports react as an untyped module. tsconfig.json pins types: [] so nothing here is auto-included as a global — only the explicit import in src/hooks resolves.
